provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
Mechanism: grey walls (original colour 5) sit on a black floor (original colour 0), with a few single seed cells in other colours. Each seed flood-fills its own 4-connected region of floor cells with its colour. Walls stop the flood, and floor regions with no seed stay unchanged.

The emitted program works directly on the visible grid. It fixes FLOOR = palette[0] and WALL = palette[5] as constants and treats every other colour as a seed. It then runs a simultaneous 4-connected BFS from all seeds over FLOOR cells. Each claimed cell gets the claiming seed's colour, and walls and seeds are never changed.

D4 handling: 4-adjacency is preserved by every rotation and reflection, and the rule has no preferred direction. So no axis or direction needs rewriting; the same neighbour set is correct in visible coordinates for every d4. Only the colour roles depend on the palette.

This reproduces the archived solver (multi-source BFS) and the generator's per-seed flood. It works on rectangular grids, handles seeds and regions on the boundary through bounds checks, and handles regions that are a single isolated seed.
draft_notes.limitations:
1. Shared regions are outside the domain: the constructor rejects any scene where two seeds' floods meet or touch. If two seeds ever shared a region, nearest-seed BFS would decide the cells, and exact ties would follow row-major seed order. That tie-break is not a rule shown by the fixtures and would need host review if such inputs were ever allowed.
2. Seed colours are distinct in the generator (random_colors), so same-colour seed merging does not come up.
3. Possible constructor defect: random_colors only excludes 5. If it could return 0, that seed would just become floor, which the generator already ignores ("color not in [0,5]"). The program treats it the same way: it is not a seed.
4. The program assumes the palette maps the original 0 and 5 to the visible floor and wall colours, as the task statement specifies. It does not infer them from the demonstrations.
5. No fixture contradictions were found. All three train pairs and the test pair match the uniform flood-fill rule.

independent_source_review.mechanism: Grey (5) walls lie on a black (0) floor, with single-cell seeds in other colours. Each seed flood-fills its own 4-connected region of floor cells with its colour. The emitted solver treats every cell that is not FLOOR=palette[0] and not WALL=palette[5] as a seed. It runs a multi-source 4-connected BFS over FLOOR cells, working directly on the visible grid.
evidence: Constructor draw(): each seed runs a stack flood. When it meets a neighbour with value in [-1, 5, own colour] it skips that neighbour. When it meets any other nonzero value it returns None, None. So any scene where a seed's region contains or touches another seed (directly adjacent, or reachable through floor) is rejected. Per-seed regions are therefore disjoint, and simultaneous BFS order cannot affect labels.
A later seed cannot overwrite an earlier seed's fill. Doing so would need a shared region, and the first seed's flood would already have hit the second seed's cell and been rejected.
'if not changed: return None' means every surviving seed colours at least one floor cell. The solver handles zero-growth seeds anyway (it leaves them unchanged), so this is not load-bearing.

Seed colours come from common.random_colors(k, exclude=[5]). This calls sample over range(1,10) minus 5, so the colours are distinct and never 0 or 5. If two seeds land on the same position the later one overwrites; this only reduces the seed count and is harmless.
Labels depend only on visible input (seed colours, wall and floor layout). There is no hidden latent, tie-break, or fixed answer.

Factory: the only specialised constants are the genuine role colours FLOOR=palette[0] and WALL=palette[5]. Output colour equals each seed's visible colour, so no arbitrary colour lookup is involved. The 4-neighbour set is D4-invariant, and there is no untransform/native-solve/retransform wrapper.
The archived transform is the same multi-source 4-connected BFS. Its final per-colour copy loop is equivalent because seed colours are distinct.

The fixtures are produced by the same draw(), so they lie inside the constructor's no-shared-region domain. Host audit passed 1000 fresh pairs, 8000 augmented checks and 16 fixture variants with no sampler rejections.
nonblocking_limits: Behaviour when two seeds share a region (nearest-seed BFS with queue-order ties) is undefined by the demonstrations. The constructor provably excludes it via the 'color != 0 -> return None' rejection.
Prior limitation 3 is moot: random_colors draws from 1..9, so it never returns 0.
The solver takes the floor and wall roles from the palette mapping rather than inferring them from the demonstrations. This is allowed specialisation of genuine rule colours.

host_review.resolution: Reviewed constructor invariants, visible-coordinate solver, fixture agreement and documented out-of-domain branches. Source hashes match passing audit.
host_review.augmentation_evidence: All eight D4 transforms are checked in audit; d4=7 is its final loop index. Palette is bijective and shared across all episode pairs.
host_review.limitations: Finite execution/domain evidence, not proof of unrestricted generalization or complete identifiability.
